svg.aria-label: buildermesh across three boxes, in five scenes: every box builds at once; a coordinator on hub-box follows leads on every box through the NATS hub and holds one before it lands until another has landed; a lead queues a check that needs macOS and only the laptop takes it; leads' asks, blocks and finishes reach your phone as push notifications; after a change lands, bmesh sync levels every box's checkout, and the sleeping laptop levels when it wakes
svg.title: buildermesh across boxes

g.text: Each box runs its own leads and executors through its own runner,
each in its own git worktree, all at once.
2. A coordinator keeps leads on every box in step.
Your coordinator session starts leads on all three boxes and follows their events through the hub;
it holds web-007 before it lands until app-012 has landed, then releases it.
3. A lead sends a check to the box that can run it.
web-007 queues mac-build, a kind with os = "darwin": the job waits on the hub
until the laptop, the one Mac, takes it, and the result comes back to web-007 as a reply.
When a lead asks, is blocked or is done, its event goes through the hub
to the daemon with ntfy set, which pushes it to your phone, once.
5. A change that lands reaches every box.
web-007 lands, which moves build-box's checkout; you run bmesh sync, which levels hub-box and sends each other box a level job.
The laptop slept through it: it levels when it wakes, and holds a new plugins commit for your approval.
hub-box runs the hub; build-box dials it; the laptop's leaf relays to it.
Events, jobs and replies on every box go through it.
bmesh hub · relays to the hub
